argument_summary: The strongest supportable position on the present admissible record is narrow certification with an explicit caveat. Aggregate launch readiness passed by 2.0 percentage points, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the public governance materials support certification decisions grounded in measurement, monitoring, and documentation of residual risk. That supports certification as an overall launch-readiness decision. The same record also shows the logistics customs triage segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points, is named in two freight customer commitments, and remains under open legal review. On that record, the admissible case is stronger for certification paired with explicit disclosure of the limitation than for unqualified certification without disclosure.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would slow the rollout path, but business cost does not cure the policy gap. The practical value of avoiding escalation is achieved here by narrowing the certification theory to overall readiness plus explicit preservation of the segment limitation, rather than pressing an unqualified non-disclosure position that the current record does not support.
claims_about_policy: The specific internal policy controls over the general public governance guidance. Under the policy text, a weakness is material when it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and product labels such as non-core do not resolve materiality when named customer commitments are involved or legal review is pending. Nothing in the admissible record resolves the named-customer issue, closes legal review, or shows approved risk acceptance. Accordingly, the policy-compliant reading is not unqualified certification without disclosure; it is certification only if the packet preserves the limitation and treats disclosure or equivalent approved coverage as required.
concessions: The current admissible record does not support treating the logistics customs triage gap as non-material.
The current admissible record does not show approved risk acceptance covering launch without disclosure.
The open legal review cannot be treated as resolved in favor of non-disclosure.
General AI governance guidance does not override the specific internal disclosure policy.
